themes.label: Withdrawals stuck, support unresponsive
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android describe deposits or winnings that cannot be withdrawn, with holds of days to weeks, unexplained account restrictions, and support emails or chats that go unanswered. Several say funds vanished or changed after a bet, and many frame the app as a scam, though the reviews mostly describe payout and support failures rather than a single identifiable bug.
themes.recommendation: Pull withdrawal and account-restriction logs for the past 90 days to measure how many users have holds over 7 days, and define an SLA with a visible status and a human escalation path for any withdrawal stuck past that threshold.

themes.label: Withdrawals blocked, AI-only support
themes.summary: Users report being unable to withdraw funds, with accounts frozen or stuck in verification, deposits sometimes charged without crediting, and payouts never arriving. Support is overwhelmingly described as automated AI replies that loop, end chats abruptly, or never escalate to a human, and email goes unanswered for days. Many reviewers say they cannot get any specific reason for the restriction or a path to resolve it.
themes.recommendation: Audit support escalation: instrument AI-to-human handoff so every chat tagged to withdrawal holds, verification blocks, or failed deposits is routed to a human agent within a set SLA, and add a visible reason code and next-step message to frozen-account notices.

themes.label: Odds volatility and bet execution
themes.summary: Users report that odds shift rapidly, so bets fail to execute or land at worse prices, often requiring several attempts on iOS and Android. Some also say displayed win percentages and predictions feel inaccurate, and a few describe losing streaks they believe are unlikely.
themes.recommendation: Investigate bet acceptance latency and price-change handling on iOS and Android by logging quote-to-execution times and rejected or repriced orders, then add a clear price-change confirmation step and audit how displayed win probabilities are calculated.

themes.label: Mixed praise and payout distrust
themes.summary: This cluster is split between enthusiastic users praising Kalshi's simple interface, easy deposits and withdrawals, and wide market variety, and frustrated users who describe slow or denied withdrawals, unhelpful support, and suspicion that rules are applied against them. Lower-rated reviews also raise thin liquidity, high fees, price slippage on live bets, and orders that disappear or cannot be cancelled. The overall average of 3.03 reflects this polarization rather than a single defect, and the complaints span both iOS and Android across several app versions.
themes.recommendation: Pull withdrawal and payout tickets from the last six months, tag each by stated reason (rule interpretation, verification hold, processing delay, support response), and publish a dashboard of median payout time by platform and app version to confirm or rule out a systemic payout problem.

themes.label: Unpaid winnings and withdrawal holds
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android say winning bets were not paid out, withdrawals were blocked or delayed, and deposits or bonuses vanished after they started winning. Many describe support as an unresponsive AI chatbot that gives generic replies, and several allege settlements were changed or misreported after the fact, with some planning lawsuits or regulatory complaints.
themes.recommendation: Audit all open withdrawal and payout tickets from the last six months, grouping them by cause (regulatory hold, deposit method block, settlement dispute, fee deduction) and by app version, then set a staffed escalation path that bypasses the chatbot for any payout over a set threshold.

themes.label: Latest update degrades trading UI
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the recent redesign removed or hid features they rely on, such as live positions, percentage chance on holdings, custom price alerts, and the 5m/15m/1hr chart intervals. Many also report slow loading, lag, stale price data, and positions not appearing until the app is reopened, which makes fast 15-minute crypto trading feel risky.
themes.recommendation: Audit the latest UI release against the prior version to list every removed or relocated element (positions card, percentage display, 5m/15m/1hr charts, custom price alerts), then restore the highest-frequency ones behind a fallback or settings toggle while investigating live-data refresh lag.

themes.label: Praise: easy navigation and variety
themes.summary: Most reviewers in this cluster are enthusiastic about how simple the app is to learn and navigate, and about the wide range of events and categories they can trade or bet on, with several saying they were placing trades within hours of first use. A few users note the trading concept was confusing at first and ask for clearer explanations of certain trades, and a couple mention the app is best approached with caution given the financial risk.
themes.recommendation: Protect the onboarding and simple layout that reviewers praise by running a usability test with new users, and pair it with an in-app explainer for trade types and odds to address the confusion some users report.

themes.label: Praise: fun, easy prediction trading
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly positive, calling the app fun, easy to use, and a way to learn about markets or trade sports outcomes. Several describe it as exciting like a lottery or sports betting, with quick payouts and cash-out options praised, though a few note the gambling-like risk and the need for self-control. Mentions of beginners learning trading and clear odds or percentage graphics recur across both Android and iOS reviews.
themes.recommendation: Protect the features users cite most (instant cash-out, payout speed, odds and percentage displays, and beginner onboarding) and add a responsible-play prompt or deposit and loss limits surfaced near the trading flow, so the fun-and-risk framing stays sustainable.

My Experience With Kalshi Addiction For a while, I convinced myself that the next trade would make up for the last loss. What started as a small amount of money and a little curiosity turned into an unhealthy habit of constantly checking markets, placing bets, and chasing wins. Every loss made me feel like I needed to win it back, and every win made me believe I could keep going. The biggest cost was not just the money I lost - it was my health, sleep, and peace of mind. I found myself staying awake late at night watching market movements, checking my phone constantly, and thinking about trades even when I should have been focusing on work, family, or personal goals. My sleep suffered because I was always worried about the next market outcome or trying to recover previous losses. Financially, the losses added up faster than I expected. Instead of accepting a loss and walking away, I often felt the urge to place another bet in hopes of recovering what I had lost. This cycle of chasing losses only made the situation worse. What began as entertainment gradually became a source of stress and anxiety. Looking back, I realize that prediction markets and betting can become addictive when they start affecting daily life, relationships, finances, and mental well-being. The constant highs and lows create a cycle that is difficult to break. I learned that no amount of chasing can guarantee a win, and the longer I continued, the more I risked losing. Today, I recognize the importance of setting limits, taking breaks, prioritizing sleep and health, and understanding that financial stability is more important than the temporary excitement of a bet. My experience taught me that chasing wins often leads to bigger losses, while stepping away can help restore balance, focus, and peace of mind.

I really wish there was a setting to reset dismissed prompts or re-enable the automatic cash-out slider after placing a trade. It seems like a simple quality-of-life feature that would help anyone who accidentally clicks “Don’t show this again.” Overall, I still absolutely love the app and would recommend it to anyone interested in prediction markets. This isn’t a complaint about the app itself - it’s just a feature request. Please consider adding a way to restore that automatic cash-out prompt because it was one of the most useful features, and I’d really love to have it back. Other than that, I genuinely think Kalshi is a fantastic app and deserves 5 stars.

So what I’m going to say here about Kalshi is not simply because I lost money. I have both won and lost on the platform, so I do not see Kalshi as inherently good or bad. But I do want to give a serious warning about what the platform really feels like from a user perspective. First, in my experience, Kalshi does not provide real customer support. I opened several tickets regarding different concerns, and not once did I feel that someone genuinely cared about understanding or resolving the issue. Most of the responses felt like copied and pasted templates that did not even address the actual question. Often, after one or two exchanges, the rest of the messages were ignored and the ticket was simply closed. The second issue is more concerning. In some markets, especially when the outcome depends on a private organization or a small information source, the timing and movements can feel suspiciously coordinated. It creates the impression that people with insider information may be participating in the same markets before the public fully understands what is happening. Whether that is true or not, my point is this: if you want to use prediction markets seriously and not simply gamble, you should be very careful about which markets you participate in. Markets tied to transparent and reliable public institutions are much safer than markets depending on small private entities or unclear information pipelines. My personal conclusion is that Kalshi functions mainly as a middleman platform. I do not personally feel that they invest enough effort into protecting users, investigating suspicious activity deeply, or creating the level of trust and fairness that many users expect from a financial prediction market. So be careful.

reviews.t: Disappointing Experience Due to Low Liquidity and High Fees
reviews.x: I've been using the Kalshi app for a while now, and unfortunately, it has been a pretty underwhelming experience. The biggest issue is the extremely low liquidity. It’s difficult to find markets with enough participants, and even when you do, the order books are so thin that getting in or out of a position without significant slippage is nearly impossible. This defeats the purpose of trying to trade predictions on real-world events, as the lack of activity makes the app feel almost unusable at times. On top of that, the fees are really high relative to what you can potentially earn. When you combine the low liquidity with the high costs, it becomes hard to justify any meaningful participation. Even if you manage to make some correct predictions, the fees eat into your profits so much that it hardly feels worth it. Overall, Kalshi has a promising concept, but with its current liquidity issues and costly fees, it’s not a platform I can recommend for anyone looking to actively trade event predictions. Hopefully, these issues get addressed, but for now, the app just doesn’t deliver.
